SOC2-A1.1: Security alert evidence does not establish capacity thresholds, utilization trends, forecasts, or scaling actions. Prepare a capacity-specific contract before approval.
SOC2-A1.3: Check that recovery exercises record results and corrective actions; a backup configuration or successful backup alone does not test recovery.
SOC2-C1.1: An inventory identifies data but does not demonstrate its protection. Require the protection decisions and tested enforcement for the same inventory scope.
SOC2-C1.2: Bind disposal proof to the confidential-data inventory, retention decisions, disposal method, and completion records; do not accept a policy alone.
SOC2-CC1.1: The governance safeguard currently asks for a CMMC system security plan. That artifact does not establish the ethical conduct commitments, reporting process, or handling of violations described by this catalog topic.
SOC2-CC1.2: Distinguish management review from board oversight. Inspect independence, oversight responsibilities, meeting decisions, and follow-up rather than granting credit for any leadership review.
SOC2-CC1.3: The roles safeguard is a more specific candidate than the broad governance safeguard. Check authority, reporting relationships, and acknowledged assignments across the assessment scope.
SOC2-CC1.4: A system security plan is not competence evidence. Prepare role requirements, hiring or assessment records, training, and remediation of identified skills gaps.
SOC2-CC1.5: A system security plan alone does not establish accountability. Examine assigned responsibilities, performance expectations, exception handling, and corrective follow-up.
SOC2-CC2.1: Specify which information supports each control decision and how completeness, accuracy, timeliness, and provenance are checked. Generic governance evidence does not establish information quality.
SOC2-CC2.2: Require records showing the relevant control information reached its intended internal recipients. A policy or system security plan without communication evidence is insufficient.
SOC2-CC2.3: Identify the external audiences, required communications, ownership, and delivery records. Internal governance documentation does not demonstrate external communication.
SOC2-CC3.1: Check that objectives are specific enough to drive risk assessment and control design; the existing CMMC-plan evidence requirement does not expressly require this.
SOC2-CC3.3: Require explicit fraud scenarios and analysis. A generic risk register may omit fraud even when its normal risk assessment workflow passes.
SOC2-CC3.4: Software change authorization does not cover all changes to the control environment. Check organizational, operational, regulatory, and technology change impacts on risks and controls.
SOC2-CC4.1: Compare the control-assessment and detection candidates separately. Monitoring security events does not by itself evaluate whether the internal control system continues to function.
SOC2-CC4.2: The remediation-plan candidate needs deficiency evaluation, escalation, accountable recipients, and closure evidence. The governance candidate's system security plan does not establish these activities.
SOC2-CC5.1: Require control selection tied to identified risks and objectives. A general governance document is not evidence of the selection and design decision for each material risk.
SOC2-CC5.2: Specify the technology control objectives, selected controls, dependencies, and operation records. The existing governance evidence requirement is too generic to settle this mapping.
SOC2-CC5.3: The policy-management candidate must cover procedure implementation and assigned responsibilities, not only policy approval or publication. Evaluate the broad governance candidate separately.
SOC2-CC6.3: Check access authorization, changes, removal, role restrictions, and review results. MFA configuration alone does not establish the complete access lifecycle.
SOC2-CC6.4: The sole candidate is change management, whose evidence concerns authorized software/infrastructure changes. This does not establish physical-entry authorization or access records. Replace the proposed relationship with a physical-access-specific candidate.
SOC2-CC6.5: The physical safeguard asks for evidence limiting facility access. It does not establish removal of residual information on retired assets. Prepare a disposal-specific candidate and verification evidence.
SOC2-CC6.6: Security detection is not the same as preventing unauthorized access from outside the system. Require boundary/access safeguards and their enforcement evidence, with detection treated as a separate contribution.
SOC2-CC6.8: A vulnerability scan does not necessarily test anti-malware protections. Identify endpoint coverage, detection/prevention configuration, update health, and response validation.
SOC2-CC7.3: Require documented event analysis, classification, and disposition. Collection of alerts without analysis cannot establish this catalog topic.
SOC2-CC7.4: Evaluate incident handling separately from privacy notification. Notification timers alone do not demonstrate incident containment, investigation, and response execution.
SOC2-CC7.5: Tie restoration and verification to actual incident scenarios. A backup record without incident recovery decisions and validation is incomplete evidence.
SOC2-CC9.1: The sole vendor-risk candidate limits evidence to vendor and partner monitoring. Business disruption can arise internally as well. Prepare continuity and risk-treatment evidence with the full scoped disruption scenarios.
SOC2-P1.1: Check current notices against the actual processing inventory and delivery to affected audiences. Review the two privacy candidates independently to avoid counting overlapping summaries as complete evidence.
SOC2-P2.1: Require traceable choices, consent status where applicable, withdrawal handling, and their enforcement in the processing workflow. A notice alone does not establish the choice mechanism.
SOC2-P3.1: Trace collected data fields and sources to stated processing purposes and the permitted collection design. An inventory alone does not establish collection limits.
SOC2-P4.1: Trace actual uses to the approved purposes and investigate deviations; a processing record that merely lists intended uses is insufficient.
SOC2-P4.2: Check retention decisions against applicable obligations and operation of expiry, exception, and hold workflows. Generic secure-disposal evidence is only part of this assessment.
SOC2-P4.3: Require completed disposal records, handling of copies, applicable exceptions, and verification that the selected disposal method operated.
SOC2-P5.1: Inspect authenticated access-request handling and fulfillment evidence, including exceptions. Generic privacy notices do not demonstrate fulfillment.
SOC2-P5.2: Inspect correction and denial decisions, requester communication, and propagation of accepted corrections. A request deadline metric alone is insufficient.
SOC2-P6.1: The broad privacy-rights candidate needs disclosure authorization and transaction records. A notice or subject-access workflow alone does not establish disclosure control.
SOC2-P6.2: Vendor monitoring does not maintain a complete disclosure ledger. Require records linked to authorizations, recipients, information disclosed, and reconciliation of completeness.
SOC2-P6.3: Neither software change approvals nor consent notices establish records of unauthorized disclosures. Prepare incident/disclosure records with completeness checks and follow-up.
SOC2-P6.4: Notification workflows do not establish third-party privacy monitoring and correction of noncompliance. Prepare supplier assurance, identified exceptions, and remediation evidence.
SOC2-P6.5: Cross-border transfer safeguards and general subject rights do not establish supplier breach-reporting commitments. Require the commitments and evidence that reporting supports the incident workflow.
SOC2-P6.6: General privacy-rights evidence does not establish breach notification. Prepare the notification decision, affected recipients, applicable timing, delivery, and exceptions.
SOC2-P6.7: Security monitoring does not establish disclosure accounting delivered on request. Prepare a reconciled disclosure ledger and requester fulfillment records.
SOC2-P7.1: Correction-request handling is only one way to find data-quality problems. Inspect preventative and detective checks and resolution of quality issues throughout processing.
SOC2-P8.1: Generic security monitoring does not establish privacy compliance monitoring. Identify privacy-specific checks, exceptions, investigation, and corrective enforcement.
SOC2-PI1.1: Inspect documented processing objectives and specifications and their approval. This is the shared safeguard's evidence anchor; do not automatically extend it to all processing stages.
SOC2-PI1.2: Input validation must address completeness and authorization as well as format checks; require reconciliation and exception evidence for the scoped input population.
SOC2-PI1.3: A processing specification does not prove execution. Require processing-run checks, reconciliations, authorization, timing, and resolved exceptions.
SOC2-PI1.4: Require output validation, reconciliation, authorized delivery, and exception handling. Do not infer correct outputs from input validation alone.
SOC2-PI1.5: Inspect retained-data integrity, completeness, retrieval, and alteration controls. A software checksum or processing specification alone does not cover every stored processing artifact.
